description_full: Federal Signal Corporation designs, manufactures, and supplies a suite of products and integrated solutions for municipal, governmental, industrial, and commercial customers in the United States, Canada, Europe, and internationally. It operates through two segments, Environmental Solutions Group, and Safety and Security Systems Group. The company offers street sweepers, sewer cleaners, industrial vacuum loaders, safe-digging trucks, dump truck bodies, and trailers, as well as waterblasting, road-marking, line-removal, metal extraction support equipment, and multi-purpose maintenance vehicles under the ELGIN, VACTOR, GUZZLER, TRUVAC, WESTECH, JETSTREAM, BLASTERS, MARK RITE LINES, HOG, NEW WAY, TRACKLESS, OX BODIES, CRYSTEEL, J-CRAFT, DURACLASS, RUGBY, TRAVIS, OSW, NTE, WTB, GROUND FORCE, TOWHAUL, BUCKS, AND SWITCH-N-GO brands; and provides refuse and recycling collection vehicles through a dealer network or direct sales to service customers. It is also involved in sale of parts, service and repair, equipment rentals, and training. The company also provides systems for community alerting, emergency vehicles, first responder interoperable communications, and industrial communications; public safety equipment, such as vehicle lightbars and sirens, industrial signaling equipment, public warning systems, and general alarm/public address systems under the Federal Signal, Federal Signal VAMA, and Victor brand names through wholesalers, distributors, independent manufacturer representatives, original equipment manufacturers, and direct sales force, as well as independent foreign distributors. In addition, the company manufactures custom liquid vacuum tank ("LVT") trucks. Federal Signal Corporation was founded in 1901 and is based in Downers Grove, Illinois.

financial_summary: Federal Signal Corporation is a mid-cap industrials business with a $7.0B market cap on $2.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 14% against a 9% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 26%.

The business throws off $227M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.03× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 24× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 1.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.6% of the shares.

sect: Its 16% operating margin runs 7pp above the Industrials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.40x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+7.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 548 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 14% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 34% and a beta of 0.94, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.39 vs 5y 0.93), so read it loosely.
About $45.3M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 31% in the 2020 crash, 27% in the 2022 bear market and 77% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $78.60 (margin of safety -47%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 32%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $51.71 to $119 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Industrials peers: P/FCF 31.0 vs 22.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 21% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.2% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 7 covering analysts target $140 on average, 21% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 14% earns above the cost of capital of 9.0%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.33).
It runs a 26% gross margin and converts 10% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.03x.
ROE of 18% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.7x equity multiplier).
It spends 0.7% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.2x net debt to EBITDA ($63.7M of cash against $564.6M of debt), with interest covered 24.2x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.6, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 137 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 15.0% over 3 years, 14.0% over 5 years and 11.0% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
At current returns, reinvesting 45% of profits supports about 6.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 16.4% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.3x depreciation (1.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.6%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 6 sales over the past year, net $3.1M sold.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.0% (0.6% in buybacks and 0.5% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years, raising it 11.9% a year over the last five.
people: With about 5,800 employees, each generates about $376K of revenue, in line with the Industrials median, and revenue has grown 7.5% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $39K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.5M (9x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
